rules.explanation: LinkedIn allows users to add up to 50 skills, but recruiters heavily evaluate the top pinned skills displayed first. Having target hard skills pinned dramatically boosts search ranking.
rules.do: Pin your top 5 core technical and industry-specific hard skills directly aligned with your target role.
rules.dont: Do not pin generic soft skills (e.g., 'Hardworking', 'Communication') in your top displayed skills list.

rules.explanation: LinkedIn's updated algorithm rewards profiles that link listed skills directly to specific work experience entries, education, or projects.
rules.do: Attach relevant skills to each specific employment or project entry under your Experience section.
rules.dont: Do not leave skills isolated strictly in the Skills section without associating them with proven experience.

rules.explanation: Endorsements on hard skills validate proficiencies to visiting recruiters and improve search relevance score.
rules.do: Secure endorsements for key technical skills from colleagues, team members, or supervisors.
rules.dont: Do not rely on unverified skills without endorsements from relevant peers or mentors.

rules.rule_name: Written Recommendations from Supervisors or Peers
rules.explanation: Profiles with written recommendations carry significantly higher credibility and help candidates stand out during final recruiter evaluation.
rules.do: Obtain at least 2–3 detailed recommendations from managers, project leads, or collaborators detailing your impact.
rules.dont: Do not leave the Recommendations section completely empty or rely only on brief, vague one-liner endorsements.
